draft.title: The Second Triumvirate
card: In 43 BC Octavian, Mark Antony and Lepidus formed the Second Triumvirate. A triumvirate is a group of three men who share power.
Unlike the informal pact of Caesar, Pompey and Crassus, this one was made legal by a law, the Lex Titia. It gave the three men wide powers for five years to reorganise the state.
They issued proscriptions: lists of enemies who could be killed and whose property was seized. This removed opponents and raised money for their armies.
In 42 BC Antony and Octavian defeated Caesar's assassins, Brutus and Cassius, at Philippi in Macedonia. This avenged Caesar and ended the main armed resistance to the triumvirs.
draft.remember: The triumvirs gained legal power, removed enemies by proscription, and won at Philippi.

a.q: Why did the triumvirs issue proscriptions?
opts: To remove their enemies and seize money for their armies
To give soldiers land in the provinces after Philippi
To pass laws that restored the powers of the Senate
To reward Caesar's heirs with gifts from his will
a.why: Proscriptions named enemies who could be killed and whose property was taken. That removed opposition and paid for the armies. They were not about restoring the Senate's powers, as the triumvirs held wide powers themselves.
a.clue: Think about what happened to the people on the lists and to their property.

b.q: Which statement best describes the Second Triumvirate in 43 BC, compared with the pact of Caesar, Pompey and Crassus?
opts: It was set up by law and gave its members official powers
It was a private agreement with no legal standing
It was formed after Philippi to share the spoils of victory
It was made up of Caesar's assassins to rule the state
b.why: The Lex Titia gave the three men legal powers for five years, which the earlier pact never had. It was not formed after Philippi: it came first, in 43 BC, and the triumvirs then fought Caesar's assassins there.
b.clue: Recall what the Lex Titia did.

a.best: To remove their enemies and seize money for their armies

b.best: It was set up by law and gave its members official powers

check.summary: No problems found. The facts on the Lex Titia, the proscriptions and Philippi are accurate, and each question has one clearly right option.
